mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions, which typically lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate positive sentiment on corporate hiring and consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where PAYEMS increases by at least 100k from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% indicates a tight labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as businesses raise prices and profits rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE falls below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by at least 0.25 percentage points and an unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.0% signals an active monetary policy response to economic weakness, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the stimulus takes effect.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by at least 0.25pp and UNRATE > 6.0%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a month-over-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals sustained economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where INDPRO increases by at least 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to the housing sector's contribution to GDP and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where HOUST increases by at least 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 2.0% annualized signals robust economic expansion, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy gains momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of quarters with GDPC1 growth above 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) by at least 1.0% and retail sales (RSAFS) by at least 0.5% signals strong consumer demand across multiple sectors, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 1.0% and RSAFS increases by at least 0.5%
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a month-over-month increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) signals accelerating inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve.
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months with CPIAUCSL increasing by at least 0.2%.
